general.label: Taxes on high incomes and wealth
general.q: When the state needs more revenue for schools or health care, should the additional burden fall more heavily on high-income earners and the very wealthy, or should tax rates stay more uniform so that successful people and businesses are not driven away?
general.a: More uniform rates that avoid driving away high earners and businesses
general.b: Higher rates or new taxes focused on high incomes and large fortunes

general.label: State spending discipline
general.q: Should California keep strict constitutional limits on how much the state can spend in good years (returning excess revenue to taxpayers or schools), or should the state be freer to expand programs when revenue is high?
general.a: Keep or strengthen firm spending limits and rainy-day rules that force restraint
general.b: Allow more flexibility so high-revenue years can fund expanded services

general.label: Housing production
general.q: To address high housing costs, should the state prioritize removing regulatory and environmental barriers so more homes of all kinds can be built faster, or prioritize targeted subsidies and requirements that guarantee affordability for lower-income households?
general.a: Remove barriers and speed approvals so the overall supply of homes rises
general.b: Focus public money and rules on subsidized or restricted affordable units

general.label: Voter identification
general.q: Should every voter be required to show government-issued identification (or provide matching ID digits on a mail ballot) to cast a counted vote, or should California continue relying primarily on signature verification without ID presentation?
general.a: Continue current rules that do not require presenting ID at the polls or on mail envelopes
general.b: Require government-issued ID for in-person voting and matching ID digits for mail ballots

general.label: Public campaign funding
general.q: Should state and local governments be allowed to use public money to fund candidate campaigns (with safeguards that education, transportation, and public-safety funds cannot be used), or should campaign funding remain private?
general.a: Keep the current ban on public funding of candidate campaigns
general.b: Allow carefully limited public financing programs

general.label: Environmental review speed
general.q: For housing, water, transportation, and clean-energy projects, should California keep the current open-ended environmental review and lawsuit process, or set firm deadlines and narrower lawsuit rules so projects finish faster?
general.a: Keep broad environmental review and lawsuit rights even if projects take longer
general.b: Impose strict deadlines and limit lawsuit scope so essential projects move faster

general.label: Borrowing for social programs
general.q: When California wants to fund large housing, research, or social programs, should it generally use general-obligation bonds that must be repaid from the state budget, or prefer pay-as-you-go or user-fee financing that does not increase long-term state debt service?
general.a: Prefer financing that does not add long-term general-fund debt service
general.b: Accept general-obligation bonds when the programs serve clear public needs

general.label: Permanent school funding
general.q: Should temporary higher income-tax rates that currently fund schools and community colleges be made permanent so the revenue stream does not expire, or should those rates be allowed to sunset so overall tax levels can fall?
general.a: Allow the temporary higher rates to expire as scheduled
general.b: Make the higher rates permanent to lock in school and college funding

general.label: Local tax approval
general.q: Should local special taxes proposed by voters continue to pass with a simple majority, or should they require a two-thirds vote the way many other local tax increases already do?
general.a: Raise the threshold to two-thirds for voter-proposed local special taxes
general.b: Keep the simple-majority threshold for voter-proposed local special taxes

general.label: Size and role of government
general.q: In general, does California need a larger, more active state government that taxes and spends more to solve housing, health, and climate problems, or a leaner government that lowers taxes and regulation so the private sector can solve more of them?
general.a: Leaner government, lower taxes and regulation
general.b: More active government with higher taxes and more programs

general.label: Recall elections
general.q: When a statewide officer is recalled, should voters choose the replacement on the same ballot, or should the vacancy be filled later by special election or appointment?
general.a: Keep the current system of choosing a replacement on the same ballot
general.b: Fill the vacancy later by special election or appointment

general.label: Overall political direction
general.q: On balance, do you prefer candidates and policies associated with the Democratic Party or the Republican Party in California?
general.a: Republican-leaning or independent of Democratic priorities

general.label: Experience vs. outsider
general.q: When choosing office-holders, do you place more weight on proven experience inside government or on fresh perspectives from outside career politics?
